finding.tls_deep.broken_ciphers: The server accepts {count} broken cipher suite(s) (no encryption, export-grade or anonymous): {examples}.
finding.tls_deep.compression: TLS compression is enabled: the server is exposed to the CRIME attack.
finding.tls_deep.legacy_protocols: Obsolete protocols accepted: {protocols}. Browsers dropped them; only very old clients need them.
finding.tls_deep.no_modern_protocol: The server accepts neither TLS 1.2 nor TLS 1.3: no safe protocol is available.
finding.tls_deep.no_pfs: {count} accepted suite(s) without forward secrecy (static RSA key exchange): a stolen key would decrypt recorded traffic.
finding.tls_deep.no_tls13: TLS 1.3 is not supported: it is faster and safer than TLS 1.2.
finding.tls_deep.sslv3: The server accepts SSLv3, an obsolete protocol vulnerable to POODLE.
finding.tls_deep.weak_ciphers: The server accepts {count} weak cipher suite(s) (RC4, DES, 3DES, MD5…): {examples}.
finding.tls_deep.weak_dh: Diffie-Hellman exchange of only {bits} bits (Logjam): use at least 2048 bits or elliptic curves.
module.tls_deep.checks: Uses partial handshakes to test the accepted versions (SSLv3, TLS 1.0 to 1.3), enumerates the cipher suites, and looks for weak or broken ciphers (RC4, 3DES, NULL, EXPORT), TLS compression (CRIME), weak Diffie-Hellman parameters (Logjam) and missing forward secrecy.
module.tls_deep.fix:
Find where TLS is terminated: web server (nginx, Apache, IIS), load balancer, CDN or application firewall. The settings are changed there; on a CDN or managed hosting, use the "minimum TLS version" and "cipher suites" options of the console.
Allow only TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3: remove SSLv3, TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.1 (see the snippet for nginx, Apache and IIS). If TLS 1.3 is missing, update the server and OpenSSL (version 1.1.1 or newer) then enable it.
Replace the cipher list with a recognised profile (the "Intermediate" profile from Mozilla and TLSRef, ANSSI recommendations): only ECDHE suites with AES-GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305. This excludes RC4, DES, 3DES, MD5, NULL, EXPORT, anonymous suites (`aNULL`) and static RSA key exchange, which has no forward secrecy.
If weak Diffie-Hellman is reported (Logjam): remove the DHE suites (the list in the snippet has none), or generate parameters of at least 2048 bits with `openssl dhparam -out dhparam.pem 2048` and declare them (`ssl_dhparam` on nginx).
If TLS compression is reported (CRIME attack): disable it (`SSLCompression off` on Apache) and update the server and OpenSSL.
On Windows (IIS), protocols and suites are handled by Schannel: apply the script in the snippet or a group policy, list the suites with `Get-TlsCipherSuite`, remove the weak ones with `Disable-TlsCipherSuite`, then restart the service or the server for the changes to apply.
Test the configuration then reload the server (`nginx -t` then `nginx -s reload`; `apachectl configtest` then `apachectl graceful`).
Check: `nmap --script ssl-enum-ciphers -p 443 example.com` must list only TLSv1.2 and TLSv1.3, with no weak suite. Then run this module again (active: use it only on your own domains).
module.tls_deep.title: Deep TLS (protocols and cipher suites)
module.tls_deep.why: A server that still accepts SSLv3, TLS 1.0 or broken ciphers lets a well-placed attacker downgrade the connection and then read or alter the traffic, even with a valid certificate.
tls_deep.score_cap: SSLv3 or broken ciphers (NULL, EXPORT, anonymous) accepted by the server
